values.job: Every time it runs (every 15 minutes is the intended schedule), turn each newly paid Stripe checkout into a customer: list the checkouts completed since the last one kept, skip any already kept, check each paid amount against a price the offer declares (a trial checkout is checked by its subscription's amount), keep a customer record keyed by the checkout, send the setup email once with an idempotency key, and mark each customer whose subscription ended as ended, keeping their record. A checkout whose amount matches no declared price is not kept; the seller is told instead. Nothing is charged, refunded or cancelled here.
values.source: {"from":"Workshop tools","name":"tools/take-payments (list completed checkouts, look up a checkout, check what a buyer paid, list ended subscriptions), tools/send-messages (send one email), the person's own store and tools/tell-the-person","note":"Made for selling through a Stripe Payment Link while no hosted app receives Stripe's webhooks: the follow-up reads Stripe instead of waiting for it. It runs on the engine's wake (a repeat every 15 minutes, starting at the first step) once wakes run recipe rows, and by hand through tools:run until then. NOT ADOPTED, with the reason: (1) granting anything from the buyer's browser landing on a success page, because a redirect can be forged; only what Stripe says counts; (2) deleting a customer's record when they cancel, because their records stay theirs; the record is marked ended; (3) sending the setup email from the seller's own mailbox without a sender they set up, so the sender and its held key are inputs."}
values.title: Give paid buyers access

values.input_schema: {"type":"object","required":["product","keywords","reddit_username"],"properties":{"product":{"type":"string","minLength":3,"description":"The person's product, in one plain sentence: what it is and who it is for"},"keywords":{"type":"array","minItems":1,"maxItems":10,"items":{"type":"string","minLength":2},"description":"The person's best keywords: the words their buyers type into Google, one phrase each"},"reddit_username":{"type":"string","minLength":3,"maxLength":20,"description":"The person's Reddit username, without u/ in front"}}}
values.job: Warm up a Reddit account before the first post: choose 5 subreddits by which ones Google ranks for the person's keywords, read and record every subreddit's rules, reach at least 10 karma, then spend 3 days leaving one useful comment a day in each of the 5 subreddits (15 comments, no self-promotion), and only then write and publish a post. The AI drafts every comment and post, the person approves the exact words, and the person sends it: the AI never posts by itself.
values.source: {"from":"X post","author":"Nicholas Dulait","url":"https://x.com/NicholasDulait/status/2115756883050918215","name":"Nicholas Dulait, X post of 2026-10-29: warm up a Reddit account for 3 days before the first post","note":"His claims, not checked here: 10 of his 12 Reddit posts went over 50K views, and the best one reached 168K. His method has 5 steps: (1) create the account with an email that is a few months old, (2) hide profile activity (Settings > Profile > Content and activity > Hide all), (3) reach at least 10 karma, (4) pick 5 subreddits that Google ranks for your best keywords, not by size, (5) for 3 days leave 1 useful comment in each of the 5 subreddits on a post from the last few hours that is gaining traction (15 comments, no self-promotion), then read every rule in the sidebar before each post. Steps 3, 4 and 5 and the rules reading are the steps of this workflow. NOT ADOPTED, with the reason: (1) using a months-old email so the account is not flagged as spam is evading spam detection, so this workflow does not use an email's age to get past a spam filter; (2) hiding profile activity so other Redditors cannot see the account is marketing conceals commercial intent, so this workflow leaves the profile as it is. The honest version is in the post steps: disclose the person's affiliation with the product wherever a subreddit's rules or Reddit's content policy require it."}
values.title: Grow on Reddit without selling for the first 3 days

Each passage used becomes or updates one of the person's source passage records (where it came from, its original words, who owns it, what use is allowed, whether it is private, what was done to it, which pieces reuse it)"},"research_kinds":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string","minLength":2},"description":"Record kinds of the person's research aids, each read if they keep it: audience guesses (competing ideas of who a piece is for, each with what would disprove it), audience cases (one real person's situation from a source), research methods (job, output, failure to avoid), a viewer worksheet or other companion asset with fill-in fields, a terms record (their words with how each was sourced), and a conflicts record (two sources that disagree and how it was treated)"},"limits":{"type":"object","description":"Record ids or files of the person's settings for each tool that needs them: render-check limits, the motion bar, speech grading settings, the camera's log profile, the look and graphics templates, the checklist schema","additionalProperties":{"type":"string"}}}},"outlier_multiple":{"type":"number","minimum":1,"description":"How many times its channel's usual views a reference must have to count as demand evidence. values.job: Make one piece of content (a video, a talk, a carousel, a post or an article) the way a careful studio would, in this order and never skipping ahead to the edit: read the person's own records, their purpose record first; describe any library row that has no crossing fields yet; find what the audience is really asking, in their own words and with where they said it, and whether they would want this; cross ALL of the person's technique, principle and format rows with that goal to get cited ideas; find what the person has already said or written that answers it; choose a format by that material and by measured references; write packages (title, cover, opening) with at least 3 hook variants to test against each other, and show them to people from the audience before making anything; build the script from those filmed points first; check every word against the person's rules and verdicts; write a shoot sheet for only what is still missing; after the person films, grade the sound, colour and cut the piece through the Workshop's tools; run every check before the person sees anything; publish; and read the numbers back to learn. Plan-time rules: every beat, title, hook and edit cites the library rows it was drawn from, and a cite that is not one of the person's rows read in this run fails the step; and every idea list, title and hook list, script and edit plan answers each test of the person's own purpose record and cites it, so audience demand only ranks ideas that already passed the person's purpose.
values.source: {"from":"the common stages of producing one piece of content (audience, idea, format, packaging, script, filming, sound, edit, review, publishing, readback), in the order that puts the audience and the idea before any editing","note":"The order and the rules are generic: research before the idea, the person's own recorded words before new lines, a source for every line, opening variants tested against each other, one decision per speech passage (use as recorded, remaster, or re-voice the same words), checks before the person is shown anything, readback at 1, 7 and 28 days with a written lesson. Purpose comes first because work judged only by demand numbers drifts away from what the person set out to do; so the person's purpose record is the first input, its tests are answered by every plan step, and demand ranks only what passed. Everything specific to a person (audience frameworks and bucket names, rubrics, pass marks, word lists, edit rules, title structures, formats, channels, tool settings) is an input read from their records at run time, never part of this recipe. A person's own checklist runs through the workflows checklist gate."}
values.title: Make one piece of content from audience to publish

values.job: When the person records a launch, read that launch record, plan the campaign backwards from its date in four phases (build the list, tease, hype and collect, blitz), write a blitz runbook in which every channel and every supporting voice posts within the first 30 to 120 minutes after the lead post, draft every post natively for its platform from one message, check every word against the person's own rules, get the person's approval of each post exactly as it will go out, schedule only approved posts in the person's own scheduler or hand them to the person, and after the launch read the numbers back against the targets the plan set. The AI drafts and schedules approved posts only; the person approves every word and owns every account.
values.produces: A dated launch calendar with its teaser, hype and blitz posts drafted per platform, and after launch a readback of what each phase brought in.

values.input_schema: {"type":"object","required":["target","goal"],"properties":{"target":{"type":"string","minLength":3,"description":"What to reverse engineer: its site address, or its name when the site is not known, for example https://example.com"},"goal":{"type":"string","minLength":5,"description":"What the person wants to grow, in their own words: their product or channel and the result they want; the plays are crossed with it"},"mode":{"type":"string","enum":["full","content","quick","funnel-hack","landscape","watch"],"default":"full","description":"full runs the whole teardown; content reads only the target's handles and own content; quick is a first look on a small budget with five plays; funnel-hack maps the whole funnel by buying through it, each action approved; landscape compares three to five competitors; watch reruns against an earlier run and reports only what is new"},"budget_usd":{"type":"number","exclusiveMinimum":0,"default":3,"description":"The most the whole run may spend from the person's treg balance, in US dollars (default 3)"},"country":{"type":"string","minLength":2,"default":"US","description":"The market to read search data for (default US)"},"account":{"type":"string","pattern":"^service_connection:treg(:[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)?$","default":"service_connection:treg","description":"Which of the person's treg connections pays"},"handles":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string","minLength":2},"description":"The target's social handles or channel addresses, if the person already knows them; the site step finds them otherwise"},"buyer_questions":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string","minLength":5},"description":"Questions a buyer asks an AI before choosing in the target's market; the search step writes three when none are given"},"models":{"type":"object","description":"The chat model tool:say-why-a-technique-works and tool:cross-techniques-with-a-goal use, as they take it ({ writing: { url, model } })"},"window_months":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"default":24,"description":"How many months back to read (default 24, or since launch when younger)"},"yours":{"type":"string","minLength":3,"description":"The person's own site, so the gap step compares stage by stage with the same vendor's estimates and their own Search Console and analytics"},"competitors":{"type":"array","minItems":3,"maxItems":5,"items":{"type":"string","minLength":3},"description":"In landscape mode, three to five competitor sites"},"previous_run":{"type":"string","pattern":"^record:calendar-task:","description":"In watch mode, the earlier run to diff against (default: the newest done run of this recipe)"}}}
values.job: For any target the person names (a company, product, app or creator): chart its monthly search traffic and brand searches from one source and find the months growth stepped up; date every launch, price change, headline change, tool added, ad start, sponsorship, campaign, funding round, press wave and hire on that chart from its site, sitemap, archives, DNS, certificate logs, ad libraries, the paid promotion ad libraries miss, posts and creator videos, founder interviews, reviews and job posts; read what it ranks for and which AI answers name and cite it; rank its own content top quarter against bottom on each channel; find its loops and programs; credit clusters of moves with their lift; compare it stage by stage with the person's own numbers and find where it is weak; then turn what worked into plays the person can copy, each with the Workshop workflow or tool that runs it and a ready prompt, plus the plays to skip and the one to start this week. Modes: full, content, quick, funnel-hack, landscape (three to five competitors side by side) and watch (only what is new since the last run). 31 industry packs adjust the signals, checks and plays. Every finding is SEEN, INFERRED, REPORTED (a founder's own claim) or NOT SEEN. Public evidence, plus first-hand use of the product only with the person's approval of each action under their own name. Free collectors run on the person's computer; every paid endpoint is priced before its first call, the run stays inside the person's budget, and after every step the person says continue, skip or stop.
values.produces: A dated growth teardown of the target with every finding labelled, its moves set against its traffic and brand searches with the lift of each cluster, the person's gap and the target's weak spots, and five to ten plays each with what runs it and a ready prompt; in content mode, the patterns that separate its best posts from its worst on each channel; in landscape mode, what is table stakes, what is a bet and what the person is missing; in watch mode, only the new moves.
values.source: {"from":["https://treg.to/skills/rea-growth/SKILL.md","https://github.com/coreyhaines31/marketingskills/tree/1f837447b20bb6f0e72d87b80ece1c221c362c7d/skills/reverse-engineer-marketing"],"name":["REA growth: turn a company's growth history into a playbook (treg)","reverse-engineer-marketing v1.1.4 by Corey Haines (marketingskills, MIT)"],"read_on":"2026-11-12","note":"Adopted: the steps and their order, full and content modes, the SEEN and INFERRED labels with 'not seen' for anything unseen, public evidence only, the price read before an endpoint's first call, free routes first, a $3 default budget, one alternative endpoint when one fails, every count computed by code and dated, and a short finding with the next check and its cost after each step, then continue, skip or stop. values.input_schema: {"type":"object","required":["niche","audience","product","own_material","platform","batch_size"],"properties":{"niche":{"type":"string","minLength":3,"description":"The page's subject in the person's own words, for example high-protein meals or budget travel"},"audience":{"type":"string","minLength":3,"description":"Who the page is for, as specifically as the person can say it"},"product":{"type":"object","required":["kind","price","currency"],"properties":{"kind":{"type":"string","minLength":3,"description":"What the product is, for example a PDF cookbook with a 7-day plan"},"price":{"type":"number","exclusiveMinimum":0},"currency":{"type":"string","pattern":"^[A-Z]{3}$","description":"ISO 4217 code, for example EUR or USD"}}},"own_material":{"type":"array","minItems":1,"items":{"type":"string","minLength":3},"description":"Where the person's own material lives: folder paths, document paths or notes they wrote, one per item"},"rival_pages":{"type":"array","maxItems":5,"items":{"type":"string","format":"uri"},"description":"Public profile addresses of the biggest pages in the niche, if the person knows them"},"platform":{"enum":["tiktok","instagram"],"description":"Where the page will post its carousels"},"batch_size":{"type":"integer","minimum":5,"maximum":120,"description":"How many carousels to draft in one batch"}}}
values.job: Build a slideshow page around the person's own material and one small paid product: list the material they really made, read the biggest pages in the niche for their top 3 formats, fix one visual style, outline the product with every item marked as the person's own or still to make, write a batch of carousels whose first slide names who it is for and whose last slide shows the product with one action, render them as 1080x1350 images, get the person's approval of every batch, schedule only approved posts, and each week read views, saves and sales, make part 2 of the winners and turn the biggest winner into a video. Every number comes from a tool call, a package label, a cited database or the person's own analytics; where there is none, the answer is "no data". The AI drafts and renders; the person approves, owns every account and the checkout, and the AI never posts by itself.
values.produces: Each Monday: which carousels won on views and saves, the part 2 of each winner, and the video of the biggest one; the before-and-after numbers are a weekly results post.
values.source: {"from":"X posts","author":"Three X posts on slideshow pages","url":"https://x.com/tivollem/status/2115760561489318295","name":"A post of 2026-10-29 on a meal-idea slideshow page that sells a EUR 4.99 cookbook (60 recipes and a 7-day plan) from its last slide, studied from its screen recording; plus Ernesto Lopez on slideshow pages (https://x.com/ErnestoSOFTWARE/status/2112940887806296269, quoted by https://x.com/ErnestoSOFTWARE/status/2115442722660037110) and on AI cooking reels (https://x.com/ErnestoSOFTWARE/status/2115897827775988205)","note":"Their claims, not checked here: the page had 462K likes with under 8K followers (the recording shows that 462K is the profile's lifetime likes; the one post shown had 1,620 likes and 635 saves); one recipe page has 488M views; 5M views brings about $2,000 to $5,000 in revenue; some sounds average about 10 times the page average. The observed format: six slides (a cover, then breakfast, lunch, dinner and dessert, one per slide, then the product), each meal slide a top-down plate, a two-line label naming the slot and three ingredients joined with '+', and three ingredient cut-outs; the last slide is the product mock-up, an outcome headline and one 'link in bio' button; the bio holds one link to a one-screen page with a single price button. The method from the article: a first slide that names who it is for and forces the next swipe; rerun a winning hook as numbered parts; one theme or character on every post; keep a sound that works; the product on the last slide and its full name in the caption; pull the biggest page's posts with views and saves, find its top 3 formats, brief 2 months, generate about 120, a person approves, schedule, and every Monday read views, make a part 2 of the winners and turn the biggest winners into video. His paid tools are replaced with open ones: ViewTrack by yt-dlp and gallery-dl metadata reads, Higgsfield by mflux image generation, Kling and Seedance by mlx-video or ltx-2-mlx, Postiz cloud by self-hosted Postiz (AGPL-3.0), and the Slack AI employee by this workflow on the person's own AI. NOT ADOPTED, with the reason: (1) AI-generated food or product photos shown as the person's own work mislead buyers, so generated images are labelled as illustrations and the person's own photos come first; (2) nutrition or health claims beyond a cited label or database are not written, because a recipe product that promises health results makes claims nobody checked; (3) bulk scraping of rival pages breaks platform terms, so rivals are read one public page at a time as metadata only and nothing is downloaded but numbers and links."}

values.input_schema: {"type":"object","required":["problem","audience","category","store"],"properties":{"problem":{"type":"string","minLength":5,"description":"The painful problem the app solves, in one sentence, as the people who have it would say it"},"audience":{"type":"string","minLength":3,"description":"Who has the problem every day"},"category":{"type":"string","minLength":2,"description":"The store category the app would sit in, for example Health & Fitness or Food & Drink"},"store":{"enum":["app-store","google-play"],"description":"Which store the app launches in first"},"competitors":{"type":"array","maxItems":5,"items":{"type":"string","minLength":2},"description":"Competing apps the person already knows, by name"}}}
values.job: Take a consumer app idea from a painful daily problem to a live subscription app: confirm that apps in the category already earn and that creators already post about the problem (stop if not), record the top 3 competitors' onboarding beats, paywall, price and growth channels from the person's own screenshots, write an onboarding that follows the winning order of beats in original words and design, end it with a paywall that states price, trial and cancellation plainly, publish a store page whose subtitle says what the app does, then run five growth channels (creators paid per post, influencers on a capped cost per 1,000 views, faceless slideshows, founder-made posts, paid ads after organic winners) with disclosures, and review installs, trials, paid users and revenue every week. Every number comes from a tool call or the person's own store and payment dashboards; where there is none, the answer is "no data". The AI drafts; the person owns the developer account, the payment setup and every contract, approves every word, and submits.
values.produces: Each Monday: installs, trials, paid users and revenue by channel, with the channel that won and why; the weekly numbers are a build-in-public post.
values.source: {"from":"X posts","author":"Ernesto Lopez","url":"https://x.com/ErnestoSOFTWARE/status/2014110519913857122","name":"Ernesto Lopez, 'I built 10 apps in 10 months' guide (X article), and his post on cooking apps and generated cooking reels (https://x.com/ErnestoSOFTWARE/status/2115897827775988205)","note":"His claims, not checked here: about $800,000 a year from 10 apps; his first app made $20,000 in its first 30 days from 2 viral videos; a recipe app at about $1M a month; a paid influencer at $1 per 1,000 views capped at $1,000; creators paid $15 a post with bonuses from $150 at 100K views to $800 at 1M. His 8 steps: validate the niche (a daily painful problem, apps already earning over $10K a month, creators already posting), build fast with AI coding tools, borrow the onboarding and pricing of the best competitors (he says he means their structure, not a literal copy, with the inside of the app original), a hard paywall at the end of onboarding, a minimal store page (clear name, a subtitle that says what it does, 3 to 5 big-text screenshots, a simple description), then five growth channels: creators, influencers, faceless slideshows with one style or character, founder-led posts, paid ads. NOT ADOPTED, with the reason: (1) copying a competitor's screens, words or design, which is copyright and trade-dress infringement, so only the order of beats is reused and every word and screen is new; (2) a paywall that hides how to close it, restore a purchase or cancel, or that charges before a clearly stated trial end, which breaks App Store guideline 3.1.2 and consumer-protection rules on subscriptions, so the paywall states price, period, trial end and how to cancel; (3) creator and influencer posts without an ad disclosure, which breaks endorsement rules, so every paid post carries one; (4) hiring a minor to send 100 cold messages a day, so outreach is done by the person or an adult they contract, one message at a time and within each platform's messaging rules."}
